hypothesis: An AI-powered skills-based recommendation engine that uses a structured skills graph and contextual behavioral signals will increase relevant engagement with learning, projects, and internal roles by at least 20% compared to a simple rule-based (non-AI) recommender, without increasing measured bias across key employee segments.

baseline.description: Rule-based recommendation engine that matches employees to learning items, projects, and roles using explicit skills tags and simple filters only.

inputs: employee_profile.skills (explicit self-declared skills and proficiency levels)
catalog_item.skills_required (for learning content, projects, and roles)
basic business rules (e.g., compliance-required training overrides)
matching_strategy: Filter catalog to items where catalog_item.role_family == employee_profile.role_family OR catalog_item.skills_required overlaps employee_profile.skills.
Score each item by count of overlapping skills between employee_profile.skills and catalog_item.skills_required.
Optionally boost items marked as 'mandatory' or 'strategic priority'.
Rank items by score descending and recency; show top N items by type (learning, projects, roles).

serving_pattern.exposure: When an employee visits the 'Recommended for You' section in the learning or internal-mobility portal, baseline logic is used if the user is assigned to the control group.
serving_pattern.randomization: Simple Bernoulli randomization at employee_id level (e.g., 50% control, 50% treatment), stratified by business unit and geography if desired.

treatment.description: AI-powered hybrid recommendation engine using skills-graph embeddings and behavioral context to recommend learning, projects, and roles.

inputs: skills_graph (nodes: skills, employees, roles, learning items, projects; edges: HAS_SKILL, REQUIRES_SKILL, LEARNED_FROM, WORKED_ON, SIMILAR_TO)
employee_profile.skills (explicit) + inferred skills from history and graph neighbors
employee_behavioral_signals (clicks, enrollments, completions, dwell time, explicit ratings)
context_signals (current role, target role interests if provided, geography, language)
global popularity and quality signals (completion rates, NPS-like ratings) with debiasing by segment

steps: Represent each skill, employee, and catalog item as an embedding vector using graph-based or matrix factorization techniques (e.g., Node2Vec on skills graph, or collaborative filtering on interaction matrix).
Construct an employee embedding as a function of their skills, past interactions, and graph neighborhood.
Construct catalog item embeddings from required skills, historical consumers, and graph neighborhood.
Compute relevance score as similarity(employee_embedding, item_embedding) plus business-rule modifiers (mandatory, strategic, compliance).
Incorporate basic diversity / fairness constraints (e.g., ensure mix of stretch vs. foundational items, cap over-exposure of any one category).
modeling_strategy.pseudocode:
import numpy as np

# Assume precomputed embeddings
emp_vec = employee_embeddings[employee_id]

def score_treatment(emp_vec, item_id):
    item_vec = item_embeddings[item_id]
    sim = np.dot(emp_vec, item_vec) / (np.linalg.norm(emp_vec) * np.linalg.norm(item_vec) + 1e-8)
    score = sim
    item = catalog[item_id]
    if item.is_mandatory:
        score += 0.3
    if item.is_strategic:
        score += 0.1
    # simple diversity penalty for over-recommended categories
    category_penalty = category_frequency_penalty(item.category)
    score -= category_penalty
    return score

scores = {item_id: score_treatment(emp_vec, item_id) for item_id in candidate_items}
recommendations = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True)[:N]

serving_pattern.exposure: When an employee in the treatment group visits the 'Recommended for You' section, treatment logic using embeddings and graph features is used.
serving_pattern.randomization: Same randomization schema as baseline for comparability.

management_overrides: Global mandatory items always appear in top K recommendations regardless of algorithmic score.
Business units may pin specific initiatives with fixed positions (e.g., slot 1 or 2), leaving remaining slots for algorithmic ranking.
explainability_hooks: Expose top 3 rationale features per recommendation (e.g., 'Because you have Skill X', 'Similar employees in Role Y took this course', 'Supports target role: Data Analyst').
Log explanation factors to enable offline audit (no impact on model).

workloads.name: learning_recommendations
workloads.description: Employees interact with recommended online courses, modules, and learning pathways.

input_data.employees_sample_size: >= 5,000 employees across at least 3 business units

workloads.name: project_matching
workloads.description: Employees are recommended internal stretch projects or gigs.

workloads.name: role_and_internal_mobility
workloads.description: Employees see recommended internal roles aligned to their skills and aspirations.

input_data.employees_sample_size: >= 3,000 employees who have viewed career pages in last 6 months
input_data.catalog_size: All open internal roles with mapped skills

stratification: gender (if legally permissible and appropriately governed)
randomization_and_assignment.procedure: Stratified random assignment such that each stratum has approximately equal representation in baseline and treatment. Assignment is persistent over the experiment window.

hold_constant: UI layout and positions of recommendation widgets (except for pinned mandatory items, which must be identical across groups).
Catalog content (no major additions or removals mid-experiment; if unavoidable, log timestamps).
Communication campaigns and nudges (e.g., same email reminders for both groups, not mentioning algorithm differences).
Eligibility rules for projects and roles.
exclusions: New hires with tenure < 30 days (insufficient behavioral history).
Employees on extended leave or with restricted system access.
Employees in jurisdictions where experimentation of this type is constrained by regulation or union agreements without prior approval.

stopping_rules: Stop early only if there is a statistically significant and practically large degradation in key KPIs (e.g., >20% drop in mandatory learning completion) in either arm.
Otherwise, run until reaching pre-specified sample size and minimum duration.

metrics.name: learning_click_through_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of recommendation impressions that result in at least one click on a learning item.

metrics.name: learning_completion_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of started learning items from recommendations that are completed within 30 days.

metrics.name: project_application_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of project recommendation impressions that lead to an application or expression of interest.

metrics.name: internal_role_click_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of role recommendation impressions that result in a click-through to role details.

metrics.name: employee_relevance_rating
metrics.definition: Average employee rating of perceived relevance of recommendations on a 1–5 Likert scale, collected via in-product survey.
metrics.calculation: Mean relevance score across all survey responses in each arm.

metrics.name: segment_fairness_gap_learning_ctr
metrics.definition: Maximum absolute difference in learning recommendation CTR between key demographic or organizational segments (e.g., gender, region) within each arm.

metrics.name: segment_fairness_gap_project_access
metrics.definition: Difference in probability of receiving at least one project recommendation per week across key segments.
metrics.calculation: Gap = max_over_segments |P(project_rec >= 1 per week | segment) - P(project_rec >= 1 per week overall)|

metrics.name: explanation_coverage_rate
metrics.definition: Proportion of displayed recommendations that are accompanied by a machine-generated explanation visible to the user.

metrics.name: explanation_trust_rating
metrics.definition: Average employee rating of whether explanations help them trust or understand the recommendation (1–5 scale).
metrics.calculation: Mean trust score from explanation-specific survey prompts.

metrics.name: override_rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of recommendations that managers or admins manually override or hide.

metrics.name: time_to_first_engagement
metrics.definition: Median time from first exposure to recommendation area until first meaningful engagement (click/enrollment/application).
metrics.calculation: Compute median (and distribution) across employees in each arm.

secondary: project_application_rate_treatment >= project_application_rate_baseline * 1.15 with p-value <= 0.10 (directional improvement acceptable).
employee_relevance_rating_treatment - employee_relevance_rating_baseline >= 0.3 on 1–5 scale with p-value <= 0.05.
fairness_and_risk_constraints: No statistically significant negative shift (p <= 0.05) in explanation_trust_rating in the treatment group compared to baseline.
executive_decision_rules: If primary criteria are met and fairness constraints are respected, recommend scaling treatment model to a broader pilot or enterprise rollout.
If performance improves but fairness constraints are violated, require model retraining or post-processing adjustments and rerun the experiment.
If performance does not improve meaningfully (<10% uplift in primary metrics), maintain baseline and iterate on model features before re-testing.
If risk metrics (override_rate, employee_relevance_rating, explanation_trust_rating) degrade notably, halt rollout and conduct qualitative diagnostics.

failure_modes.name: cold_start_employees
failure_modes.description: Employees with limited historical data receive poor or generic recommendations.
mitigations: Fallback to baseline rule-based recommendations when interaction history is below a minimum threshold.
Leverage explicit skills profiles and role-family priors more heavily for these users.
Implement a short onboarding questionnaire to gather immediate preference and goal signals.

failure_modes.name: cold_start_items
failure_modes.description: New learning items or projects with no interaction history are under-recommended.
mitigations: Use content-based embeddings from skills_required and descriptions to seed item embeddings.
Apply temporary exploration boost for new items until a minimum number of impressions/clicks are recorded.
Monitor exposure parity for new strategic items via dashboards.

failure_modes.name: feedback_loop_bias
failure_modes.description: Popular items become more popular, and niche or segment-relevant items are rarely surfaced, reinforcing existing patterns and potential biases.
mitigations: Introduce controlled exploration (e.g., epsilon-greedy) to show lower-ranked items occasionally.
Regularly re-normalize popularity features by segment to prevent overfitting to majority segments.
Audit exposure and engagement metrics by segment on a recurring schedule.

failure_modes.name: segment_disparities
failure_modes.description: Certain demographic or organizational segments systematically receive lower-quality or fewer recommendations.
mitigations: Compute fairness metrics (CTR and access gaps) and include them in experiment monitoring.
Apply post-processing re-ranking to enforce minimum exposure quotas for under-served segments where legally permissible.
Engage ethics and legal review if disparities persist; adjust feature sets or modeling approach.

failure_modes.name: explanation_mismatch
failure_modes.description: Displayed explanation does not accurately reflect the real drivers of the recommendation, reducing trust.
mitigations: Align explanation generation with actual model features used in scoring (e.g., top contributing skills or interactions).
Run internal QA comparing logged feature attributions to displayed explanations.
Collect explicit feedback ('This explanation is helpful / not helpful') and iterate on templates.

failure_modes.name: data_quality_issues
failure_modes.description: Incorrect or outdated skills profiles or catalog tags lead to irrelevant matches.
mitigations: Implement pre-experiment data checks for missing or inconsistent skills data.
Allow employees and managers to suggest corrections to skills profiles and tags with workflow approvals.
Track a 'data issue' feedback flag for any recommendation and route to content owners.

failure_modes.name: organizational_pushback
failure_modes.description: Managers or employees distrust algorithmic recommendations, leading to low adoption regardless of underlying quality.
mitigations: Position the system as decision support rather than automation of decisions.
Provide clear communication about what the system does and does not do (e.g., not used for punitive performance evaluations).
Involve representative managers and employees in early pilot feedback sessions.

minimum_fields_employee: skills (list of skill_ids with optional proficiency levels)
optional_demographics (e.g., gender, age_band) subject to legal and ethical approvals

infrastructure.application_layer: Web-based or intranet portal with authenticated employee access and the ability to render recommendations via API.
services: Treatment recommendation service endpoint with embedding lookup and scoring.
Experiment assignment service (feature flag / A/B testing platform) supporting employee_id-based bucketing.
storage_and_computing: Relational or columnar data store for employee and catalog metadata.
Graph database or equivalent structure (optional but recommended) for the skills graph.
Computation environment for training embeddings (e.g., Python environment with libraries like pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, PyTorch or TensorFlow; or equivalent).
analytics_stack: Data warehouse or lake for experiment logs (e.g., SQL-capable).
Dashboarding/BI tool to visualize metrics by arm and segment.
Statistical analysis environment (e.g., Python/R notebooks) for experiment evaluation.

approvals: People analytics lead and CHRO consent for experimentation on employees.
Legal and data privacy review for use of demographic data in fairness analysis.
Works council/union consultation where required by jurisdiction.
policies: Clear documentation that recommendations are advisory, not determinative for performance management.
Data retention policy for logs and models.
Employee-facing privacy notice describing data usage and the existence of recommendation algorithms.

1_data_preparation: Extract employee, catalog, and interaction data according to the required schema and store in a secure analytics environment.
Normalize skills identifiers across systems (HRIS, LMS, project systems) into a unified skills ontology.
Construct the skills graph using nodes (skills, employees, items, projects, roles) and edges (HAS_SKILL, REQUIRES_SKILL, LEARNED_FROM, APPLIED_TO, SIMILAR_TO).
Validate data completeness (e.g., percentage of items with skills_required, percentage of employees with at least one skill) and resolve critical gaps before proceeding.
2_model_and_baseline_implementation: Implement the baseline rule-based recommender as a stateless function or microservice using the matching strategy described in the baseline section.
In the companion repository, provide a reference implementation (e.g., Python + SQL) that can be adapted to the organization’s environment.
For the treatment, train embeddings using either graph-based methods (e.g., Node2Vec) or collaborative filtering, following code patterns in the repository.
Persist embeddings for employees and catalog items in a lookup store accessible to the treatment recommendation service.
3_experiment_design_and_assignment: Define the target employee population (e.g., knowledge workers in selected BUs) and apply exclusion criteria.
Choose randomization ratios (default 50/50) and stratification variables (e.g., BU, region, seniority).
Configure the experiment in the feature flag or A/B testing platform to assign each employee_id to baseline or treatment persistently.
Simulate assignment on historical data to validate balance across strata.
4_integration_and_ui: Expose a unified recommendations API that accepts (employee_id, context) and routes to baseline or treatment service based on experiment assignment.
Ensure the UI for recommendations is identical for both groups except for the underlying algorithm, including positions, labels, and call-to-action buttons.
Implement logging hooks to capture all required interaction events, including experiment arm and recommendation rank.
Add optional unobtrusive prompts in the UI to capture employee_relevance_rating and explanation_trust_rating.
5_pilot_execution: Soft-launch the experiment with a small internal group (e.g., one BU) to validate end-to-end data flow and logging for 3–5 days.
Check that assignment proportions and stratification are as expected.
Verify that mandatory items, business rules, and pinned items behave identically in both arms.
If checks pass, expand to full targeted population and start the formal experiment clock.
6_monitoring_during_run: Daily (or weekly) monitor core safety metrics by arm (e.g., mandatory training completion, system errors, override_rate).
Weekly, compute preliminary engagement metrics (CTR, completion) and fairness gaps for internal monitoring only (no peeking-driven changes unless risk thresholds are breached).
Log and investigate any significant system failures or spikes in override_rate or negative feedback.
7_post_experiment_analysis: After reaching the predetermined sample size and minimum duration, freeze the experiment and extract interaction logs by arm.
Compute all defined metrics overall and stratified by key segments.
Perform statistical tests (e.g., difference-in-proportions z-tests for CTR and completion, t-tests or non-parametric tests for ratings) to estimate effect sizes and confidence intervals.
Evaluate fairness constraints and override_rate, and document whether success criteria are met.
Prepare an executive summary with performance vs. baseline, fairness outcomes, and recommended next steps (scale, iterate, or revert).
8_reproducibility_and_repository: Use the companion repository (https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-executive-upskilling-playbook) to version-control all experiment code: data preparation scripts, model training notebooks, recommendation services, and analysis notebooks.
Store experiment configuration (e.g., randomization seeds, feature sets, hyperparameters) in a machine-readable config file (e.g., YAML or JSON) checked into the repo.
Document each experiment run with an experiment_id, date range, population description, and links to dashboards or analysis notebooks.
Ensure all scripts can be re-run on a synthetic or anonymized dataset to validate the end-to-end pipeline without accessing sensitive real employee data.

fields.skills: array of {skill_id: string, proficiency_level: optional integer}
fields.demographics: optional object with fields such as gender, age_band where legally permissible and anonymized

fields.explanation_features: optional array of strings (e.g., skill_ids or rationale codes)

fields.statistical_tests: object (e.g., p-values and effect sizes comparing arms)

reproducibility_requirements: All transformations from raw entities to derived_metrics_dataset must be defined in versioned scripts or pipelines in the companion repository.
Configuration for a given experiment (e.g., time window, inclusion criteria, segment definitions) must be captured in a machine-readable config file associated with the experiment_id.
Synthetic or anonymized example datasets following this schema should be included in the repository to allow dry-run execution of the analysis pipelines without production data.
